# Review of beowulf-fitt-19 (lines 1251–1320)

Units are cited by starting line; "1251a" is the one-line unit "Sigon þā tō slǣpe.", "1251b" the unit "Sum sāre angeald…".
Severity: major = a false grammatical label or a wrong sense; moderate = omission, misleading rendering, false cross-reference or unsupported claim; minor = wording or consistency.
`t` untouched (checked: all 30 `t`, `ln`, `v`, `p` identical to the draft; `i` present on all 30). No gloss.json existed for this part, so no parse could be checked against one.

## Pass 1 — notes: every label true of its form in its line; every placement claim checked; no note contradicting its `l`/`i`

| line | field | severity | what was wrong | what was done |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1251b | n | moderate | Said the published parts render ‘warode’ as ‘warded’/‘kept’ at fitt 1 line 104; that line has ‘weardode’ (weardian), a different verb | Reworded: close in sense to ‘weardode’ (rendered ‘warded’), ‘warian’ and ‘weardian’ named as different verbs |
| 1258 | n | minor | Quoted ‘dreadful waters’ but `i` says ‘terrible waters’ | Note now quotes ‘terrible waters’ |
| 1263 | n | minor | ‘held the wasteland’ against `l` ‘warded’ | Now ‘warded (kept) the wasteland’ |
| 1265 | n | moderate | Attributed to Klaeber the reading of ‘geōsceaft-’ as old ‘gesceaft’; the apparatus gives it to Kluge and Holthausen | Attribution corrected |
| 1266 | n | minor | ‘heoru’ glossed ‘sword’ only, while 1282 reads it ‘blade’ | ‘sword, blade’ |
| 1270 | n | minor | ‘strenge’ labelled flatly genitive; the form serves for genitive, dative, accusative | Label widened, role (object) stated |
| 1282 | n | major | ‘wǣpnedmen’ called dative plural; it is the dative singular of ‘mann’ (mutated vowel) | Label corrected; ‘beside an armed man’ |
| 1282 | n | minor | ‘geþrūen’ credited to Sievers alone; apparatus has Grein (query) and Sievers | Both named |
| 1290 | n | minor | ‘ongietan’ glossed ‘take hold of’, not a sense of the verb | ‘perceive, grasp’; ‘seized’ left flagged as loose |
| 1296 | n | minor | ‘a fixed epithet’ for ‘blǣdfæstne’ implied a formula not shown | ‘an accusative in apposition to ‘þone’’ |
| 1302 | n | moderate | Hand “seen hanging in the hall at line 925” is wrong; 925 is only the fitt’s first line. Hand left at 970, seen under the roof at 983 (checked in source and fitt 14) | Citation corrected |
| 1302 | n | moderate | Stated flatly that the hand is the son’s, then said that is an inference | Now “probably the arm and hand of her son” |
| 1306 | n | minor | “three accusatives … and ‘dēadne’” miscounted four items and put the noun among the modifiers | Object ‘aldorþegn’; the other three agree with it |
| 1310 | n | moderate | ‘būr’ called “his lodging, of the last unit”; the last unit has no lodging, and the king is the one waiting in the next | Says whose chamber is not given; the king’s bower likely |
| 1316 | n | minor | ‘army-worthy’ against `l` ‘war-worthy’ | Note matches `l`, ‘fyrd’ explained |

| 1319 | n | moderate | “the night summons of Hrothgar” invented a content for ‘nēodlaðu’ | Replaced: who invited whom is not said |

Pass 1 counts: major 1, moderate 6, minor 10 (17 changes).

Pass 1 findings considered and refused:
- 1251a: “the Danes and Geats who have bedded down” — fitt 18 (1237–1250) ends with men guarding and the hall prepared for sleeping; the claim is a fair summary. Kept.
- 1255: ‘lange þrāge’ called an accusative of time; þrāg is feminine, accusative form fits, and a dative would give the same sense. Kept.
- 1258: ‘galgmōd’ as ‘gallows-minded’ cannot be tested against anything outside the lexica; the note already hedges and cites Bosworth–Toller. Kept.
- 1276: ‘sunu’ as genitive; the apparatus (suna or sunu dēað) supports it and the note says it is Klaeber’s reading. Kept.
- 1279: ‘Hring-Dene’ “of line 116” — correct (the word stands in 116; published fitt 2 starts that unit at 115). Kept.
- 1288, 1292, 1294, 1304, 1306 and the remaining notes: every other label checked against its form and line and found true.

## Pass 2 — Old English to `l` word by word; `l` and `i`; remembered English; consistency with the published parts

| line | field | severity | what was wrong | what was done |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1258 | l | moderate | ‘sē þe’ is masculine (the note says so) but `l` read “she who” | “he who”; `i` keeps “she who” |
| 1258 | i | moderate | “brooded on her misery” is a remembered famous-translation phrase; ‘gemunde’ is “remembered” | “who remembered her misery” |
| 1258 | i | moderate | ‘fæderenmǣge’ (apposition to ‘brēþer’) rendered as if it described Cain | “the slayer by the sword of his only brother, his kinsman on the father’s side” |
| 1269 | l | minor | “became a grasper” made ‘ætgrǣpe’ a noun; note and glossing treat it as adjective | “became gripping” |
| 1270 | i | minor | “generous gift” against note’s ‘ample/splendid’ for ‘gimfæste’ | “splendid gift” |
| 1274 | i | moderate | “to see his dwelling of death, the enemy of mankind” read as apposition to the dwelling | Reordered: “the enemy of mankind went away, humbled and robbed of joy, to see his dwelling of death” |
| 1276 | l | minor | “would go” blurred ‘wolde’ (wished); note says ‘wished to go’ | “wished to go” |
| 1282 | l | major | “by armed men” plural for ‘be wǣpnedmen’ (dative singular) | “by a weaponed man”; agrees with `i` “an armed man’s” |
| 1282 | l | moderate | ‘heoru’ “sword” and ‘sweord’ “blade” were the reverse of `i` and note | ‘heoru’ blade, ‘sweord’ sword |
| 1290 | i | minor | “None of them … took hold of him” mixed plural and singular | “When the terror took hold of him, each man gave no thought to helmet or broad mail-coat” |
| 1302 | i | moderate | “snatched back” added “back”, not in ‘genam’ | “took the hand she knew from under the gore” |
| 1311 | l | moderate | ‘him’ (‘hwæþer him Alwalda…’, dative, the king) omitted from `l` and `i` | “whether for him the All-ruler…”; `i` has “for him” |
| 1311 | l | minor | “woe-tidings” against note ‘woe-tale’ | “woe-tale” |
| 1311 | i | moderate | “himself one of the earls” misattached ‘self’ (it goes with “with his companions”); “to learn whether” made Beowulf the one waiting to see | Rewritten: the king “waited to see whether…”; ‘self’ with the champion |
| 1311 | n | minor | Note did not mention ‘him’ | Added, so note, `l` and `i` agree |
| 1316 | i | minor | “picked band” — ‘picked’ is not in ‘handscale’ | “band of followers” |
| 1319 | l | minor | “invitation” singular for ‘nēodlaðu[m]’ (dative plural) | “invitations” |
| 1319 | i | moderate | “had passed a comfortable night after the urgent summons” sounds like a published translation and adds “summons” | Rebuilt: “whether the night had been an easy one for him, after such pressing invitations” |

Pass 2 counts: major 1, moderate 9, minor 8 (18 changes).

Pass 2 findings considered and refused:
- 1270 `l` “in the Sole-ruler” for ‘tō Anwaldan’: ‘tō’ is “to”, but “trusted to” is not English; coherence wins ties (conventions). Kept.
- 1280 `l` “was a reversal” for ‘wearð’: published parts use “came”/“became”/“was” by context; kept.
- 1303 `i` “the homes of the Danes”: ‘of the Danes’ is context, sense-harmless. Kept.
- 1311 `l` “would” for ‘wille’ (present subjunctive): sequence in a clause after a past verb; kept.
- 1290 `i` “took hold of him” for ‘angeat’: note flags ‘seized’ as loose; no better English for the idiom. Kept.
- 1258 `l` “awesome-woman” and ‘āglǣca’ “awesome one” agree with published fitts 6, 8, 11, 13, 15; ‘ides’ “lady” agrees with 9, 16, 17; ‘mancynnes fēond’, ‘Ingwine’, ‘Alwalda’ (“All-ruler”) agree with fitts 2, 15 and 14. Kept. No remembered-translation phrases left in `i`; “strength of his might” and “no good bargain” rebuild from the grammar.
- 1260 and 1281 note vs `i`: ‘fealh’ kept without emendation, consistent with the apparatus (1200b ‘flēah’ proposed only there).

Not within this review but worth the owner’s eye: the shared glossary key ‘hēan’ is entered only as ‘hēah’ (dative singular, ‘in the high hall’); the form at line 1274 (‘hēan gewāt’, nominative singular, “abject”) is a different word, so the reader’s lookup there is wrong. Needs a broadened glossary entry (`__broaden__`), not a unit edit.

## Gloss check

Every novel form (122) and every known form (163) was checked against each line where it occurs. All 11 original `__broaden__` entries are the old glossary entry whole + ' · ' + the new reading (checked against `beowulf-glossary.json`); all 15 are now. No novel key is already in the glossary; no form of the 70 lines lacks an entry; no line numbers or "here" in any entry.

| key | change | severity | reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| wer | `__broaden__`: accusative singular, object of ‘findan’ | major | Glossary has only the nominative; ‘wæccendne wer’ (1268) is accusative, so the reader's lookup gave a false parse |
| āngan | `__broaden__`: weak dative singular masculine | major | Glossary has only accusative singular feminine; ‘tō ecgbanan āngan brēþer’ (1262) is masculine dative, agreeing with ‘brēþer’ |
| ǣfenræste | `__broaden__`: dative singular | moderate | Glossary says accusative; ‘angeald’ takes the dative of the thing paid for, and the unit note says the form does not show its case |
| sunu | `__broaden__`: genitive singular (Klaeber's reading) | moderate | Existing readings are acc., dative-in-sense, nom., voc.; the note and `l` take ‘sunu dēoð’ as ‘the son's death’ |
| galgmōd | first element ‘galga’ ‘gallows’, ‘gloomy’ as the lexicon's sense | moderate | Entry said ‘galg’ ‘gloomy, sad’ as the element, contradicting the unit note and `l` (‘gallows-minded’) |
| wōc | ‘subject is fela with a genitive’; lemma ‘wacan’, also listed ‘wæcnan’ | moderate | Said “plural subject fela” (fela is indeclinable, the verb singular); note names ‘wæcnan’, entry only ‘wacan’ |
| gīfre | dropped “related to giefan” | moderate | Unsupported etymology (‘giefan’ ‘give’ is another root) |
| geþrūen | removed ‘þrīn-’ guess, aligned with the note (rare verb, perhaps ‘press, force’) | minor | Unsupported cognate; entry and note disagreed |
| handscale | ‘picked band’ → ‘band of retainers’ | minor | ‘picked’ is not in ‘handscalu’ (review pass 2 removed it from `l`/`i`/note) |
| nēodlaðum | ‘urgent summons’ → ‘urgent invitation’; case given as dative plural | minor | ‘summons’ removed from the unit in pass 2; case label left the number open |
| hrēon | ending -n noted as standing for -m | minor | Strong dative singular neuter is ‘hrēom’; the form needs the remark |
| gēate | “agreeing with mǣrum” → “modified by mǣrum” | minor | ‘Gēate’ is the noun, ‘mǣrum’ the adjective |

Counts: major 2, moderate 5, minor 5 (12 changes: 4 new `__broaden__`, 8 edited entries).

Gloss findings considered and refused:
- ‘lǣssa’ (weak nominative of a comparative, predicative): comparatives are weak throughout; kept.
- ‘niht’ (1320, nominative): the known entry says only “singular”, which covers it; kept.
- ‘ōþer’ (1300): the known entry already has nominative singular neuter; kept.
- ‘gife’/‘strenge’ “object of gemunde”: consistent with the unit note (gemunde may take the accusative); kept.
- ‘heorowearh’ “applied to Grendel”, ‘wīfes’ example phrase: context labels, not line numbers or “here”; kept.
- ‘hēan’, ‘be’, ‘cræft’, ‘cūþe’, ‘fāh’, ‘gif’, ‘gryre’, ‘strēamas’, ‘sweord’, ‘sīde’, ‘sē’: the drafted broadenings were each checked at every occurrence and are correct; the earlier review note about ‘hēan’ is resolved.
